assessments.reasoning: SPDX’s json/details/AFL-3.0.json gives licenseId AFL-3.0, name Academic Free License v3.0 and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Its crossRef and seeAlso list http://www.rosenlaw.com/AFL3.0.htm and https://opensource.org/license/AFL-3.0.

The SPDX repository’s annotated v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the AFL-3.0 detail URL. The upstream API reports an unsigned tag and identifies the target separately from the tag object.

OSI CMS record 366 links its public /license/afl-3-0 page, gives version 3.0 and displays AFL-3.0. Its rendered application notice confirms the named edition across the different URL spellings and representations.

challenge.method: Matched the tag target to the detail path and checked the ID, name, deprecation flag and two reference routes against OSI’s CMS fields. Examined the apparent disagreement in approval metadata.
challenge.results: The Rosenlaw cross-reference has match “false” and the OSI reference has match “N/A”. The CMS title, version, displayed identifier and notice still agree on AFL-3.0. SPDX isOsiApproved=true and OSI CMS approved=false leave approval history unresolved without affecting this membership claim.

limitations: The Rosenlaw URL and OSI public-page URL were inspected as fields of the SPDX detail. The directly inspected publisher representation was CMS record 366. Legal-text equality, compatibility, work-specific applicability and approval history require separate evidence.
reasoning: The pinned SPDX detail assigns AFL-3.0 to Academic Free License v3.0. OSI’s CMS independently identifies the edition in the operative notice and displays the same SPDX identifier.
